1 big thing: Cancer vaccine trial shows promise
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

A new personalized mRNA treatment from Moderna and Merck prevented skin cancer from recurring or spreading in a late-stage trial, Axios' Tina Reed reports.

  • The results could help lift the cloud hanging over mRNA technology, after Trump administration health officials cut federal funding and asserted that it poses more risks than rewards.

🔬 The experimental therapy, called intismeran, was tested in combination with Merck's cancer drug Keytruda in more than 1,100 patients with high-risk melanoma that had been surgically removed.

  • The combination demonstrated a "clinically meaningful improvement" over treatment with Keytruda alone.

🧬 The mRNA-based drugs train the immune system to find mutations that cause tumors.

  • That's in contrast to chemotherapy, which damages or destroys cancer cells.

Moderna President Stephen Hoge tells Axios: "I do hope that this will move people away from pigeonholing mRNA as a vaccine platform, or maybe even more incorrectly, tying it to the things they didn't like about the pandemic era that had nothing to do with the technology."

  • "I hope this starts to move us past that because it is, we think, a transformational moment in cancer."

📊 What's next: The full results of the trial will be released at an upcoming medical meeting.

2. 🇸🇾 Syrian foreign minister: Israeli bombing unjustified
 
Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photos: Tom Nicholson, Antonio Masiello, and Ula Muhammed/Anadolu via Getty Images

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani made it clear to Israel that his government wasn't working with Turkey to amass a military presence at a Syrian airbase — but Israel attacked the site anyway, he tells Axios' Barak Ravid.

  • The Tuesday morning strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase has heightened tensions among three close U.S. partners in the region, just as the Trump administration is trying to prevent further escalation.

🇹🇷 Al-Shaibani tells Axios: "[T]here was no intention to establish a Turkish base there, nor to establish a permanent Turkish military presence or deploy Turkish forces at the site."

  • President Trump told Axios in a phone call yesterday that he'd been briefed on the Israeli strike, but declined to comment on it. "I can't talk about it," he said.

💥 Israel dropped at least eight bombs at the base in northern Syria, about 45 miles from the Turkish border.

  • The strike damaged the runways, which had recently been rebuilt. There were no casualties.

4. 🍸 1 for the road: Union Station's glam new bar
 
Photo: Albert Ting/Continental Club

A fancy new cocktail bar just pulled into Washington's Union Station, Axios D.C.'s Anna Spiegel reports.

  • Continental Club, a lofty cocktail lounge at the station's soaring Beaux-Arts Main Hall, opens today through the end of the year.

🚂 Founder Rochelle Julich tells Axios that the narrow rooms overlooking the station reminded her of train cars, inspiring a look modeled after vintage parlor cars and refreshments that nod to the "Golden Age of Rail."

  • Think mahogany, brass and blue velvet, with Union Station's gilded architecture and historic Legionnaire statues as the backdrop.
Photo: Albert Ting/Continental Club

🥃 The drink menu riffs on Prohibition-era classics like Bee's Knees and Manhattans, alongside modern spins like a cucumber-basil Capitol Gimlet.

  • Bar bites include fried chicken biscuit bites, truffle popcorn and "railway style" hot dogs with mustard, relish and onions.
